Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)
- 1) Atopic dermatitis (eczema) flare
  - Likelihood: High
  - Justification: Known history of eczema; widespread involvement (chest, hands, inner elbows); pruritus and dryness with recent worsening consistent with an eczema flare.
- 2) Allergic contact dermatitis / irritant dermatitis
  - Likelihood: Medium
  - Justification: Widespread pruritus with dermatitis could reflect exposure to an allergen or irritant; clarified exposure history not provided in transcript.
- 3) Scabies
  - Likelihood: Low to Medium
  - Justification: Pruritus with involvement of elbows could fit scabies in some cases; lack of classic features (burrows, nocturnal itch) reduces likelihood.
- Note: Other dermatologic etiologies (e.g., xerosis related to dryness; endocrinologic factors) considered but less likely given the clinical presentation and acute flare pattern.
